title: T3 — Tesla valve
request: A Tesla valve: a straight main channel with four teardrop-shaped bypass loops branching off it and rejoining it downstream, so that flow one way runs straight through and flow the other way is diverted into the loops and opposes itself. Channel width 6 mm, overall length about 120 mm, plane (2D). Inlet at one end, outlet at the other.
properties: channel width, 6 mm, in the main channel and in a loop
**every loop both branches from and rejoins the main channel** — the fluid domain is one connected region with no isolated pocket and no loop that dead-ends
the mesh is one cell thick with both side patches `empty`

run.tail:
n `/work/20260911-115250-b0e0/bash-t3`:

**Geometry model** (`build_tesla.py`, self-contained and re-runnable):
- Straight main channel, 6 mm wide, ~120 mm long (10 mm inlet straight + 4×22 mm loop stages with 2 mm gaps + 16 mm outlet straight).
- 4 teardrop-shaped bypass loops, alternating top/bottom of the main channel, each built in gmsh's OCC kernel as: a teardrop-outline bulge fused onto the duct (via boolean `fuse`, with a point-order fix I had to find by trial — OCC's fuse only merged the bulge into one face when the loop's winding matched the duct's; the same code mirrored for a bottom loop worked immediately, a top loop needed the point order reversed), then an elliptical **island cut out of the middle** of each bulge, so the bypass is a genuine channel wrapped around a solid obstacle — narrow necks at the branch/rejoin points, not just an open side-pocket.
- Extruded one cell thick in z with `recombine=True` (needed once the base mesh isn't quad-only, else OCC tetrahedralizes the volume and `checkMesh` complains it isn't recognizably 2D), both z-faces typed `empty`.

**Mesh**: converted with `gmshToFoam`, walls retyped `wall`, ends kept as `inlet`/`outlet` patches (picked out automatically by x=0 / x=L bounding boxes after the boolean ops, since OCC doesn't preserve tags through fuse/cut). Background cell size ≈ 0.6 mm (10 cells across the 6 mm channel width).

**Result**: 4,234 cells, `checkMesh` verdict **Mesh OK** — max non-orthogonality 23.6°, max skewness 0.44, max aspect ratio 2.24, boundary closed and openness ~1e-16. Picture (`look.png`, also on your screen) confirms the shape and that inlet/outlet patches are on the ends you'd expect.

What I did **not** do: no flow solve, no BCs, no check that the loop geometry actually produces meaningful diodicity (that needs a solve to verify) — this was scoped as geometry + mesh only. The loop shape is a simplified teardrop (smooth bulge + elliptical island), not a hand-tuned diode-optimized profile; if you want it closer to a specific published Tesla-valve geometry (sharper point at the rejoin neck, different loop-to-main width ratio), I can adjust the parameters in `build_tesla.py` — they're all named constants at the top of the file.
